A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text and appendices describing the same advective-diffusion Transformer work. The architectures, equations, experiments and figures can be matched despite substantial rewriting and renaming.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations on information networks, molecular properties, protein interactions and molecular mapping.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments, Arxiv/Twitch comparisons, protein regression results and molecular mapping evaluations, including appendix results.

M1.justification: ADiT-INVERSE/SERIES become AdvDIFFormer-I/S, but retain the same precomputed global attention, adjacency-based advection, inverse/series implementations, encoders, decoders and edge-feature extensions. v1 Equation 8 and v2 Equation 6 describe the same proposed dynamics.

E1.justification: Reported evaluation coverage contracts: v1's OGB-BACE/SIDER property-prediction experiments and protein link-prediction evaluation have no corresponding results anywhere in v2. Their names persist in v2's dataset table and protein setup, but reported protein tasks are restricted to node/edge regression. Synthetic shifts, Arxiv/Twitch and HAM molecular mapping remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds MLP comparisons on Arxiv, Twitch and protein regression, plus A-DGNs and CDE on Arxiv/Twitch, including per-network Twitch results. These substantially broaden the comparisons with feature-only controls and closely related differential-equation models absent from v1's corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Synthetic evaluation changes from RMSE by dataset index to MSE versus adjacency differences in Figure 3. Protein regression adds explicit average and worst-test-graph metrics. The documented splits, hyperparameter searches and training-selection procedure otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain the substantially revised protein scores through changed settings.

E4.justification: v1's molecular edge-feature ablation in Table 10 is removed. v2 adds worst-graph protein regression analysis, examining performance across heterogeneous test networks. The Arxiv component ablations, beta/K/theta sensitivity studies and molecular mapping case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent trials and reporting means and standard deviations in tables and figures. No additional repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Protein regression results are substantially replaced: the series variant's test node RMSE changes from 1.49±0.03 to 0.574±0.028, and edge RMSE from 0.144±0.001 to 0.167±0.004. GraphTrans changes from OOM to numerical protein results. v2 also adds baseline/worst-case entries, revises the Arxiv no-advection ablation and removes molecular-property, link-prediction and some Arxiv training/validation results. Full-model Arxiv/Twitch and HAM scores remain unchanged. The cause of the protein revisions is undocumented.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 3.1 replaces v1's generalization bound with separate in-distribution, model-sensitivity and label-shift terms; the in-distribution term now uses Rademacher complexity. Theorem 3.2 adds injectivity of feature generation. Appendix B introduces a noncommuting matrix-exponential perturbation lemma and substantially rewrites the proofs. The local-diffusion bound gains a perturbation-norm prefactor, while v1's dedicated time-dependent-diffusion proposition and proof are removed.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a physics-derived Transformer with topological-generalization guarantees and broad empirical superiority. v2's introduction refines the criticism of local diffusion into an exponentially growing error upper bound, whereas v1 foregrounds exponential sensitivity. Conditional generalization of non-local diffusion remains in the paper but is no longer highlighted separately in the abstract.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes model-controllable sensitivity from label changes determined by data generation, materially qualifying the interpretation of generalization control. Section 3.4 explicitly cautions that an exponential upper bound does not guarantee exponential error growth in practice and explains when sensitivity is harmful. The earlier outlook and applicability limitations are largely retained in Appendix G.

D1.justification: v2 removes the detailed molecular-property preprocessing, edge-attribute and public-split description, and drops v1's promised public-code-release statement. Neither PDF supplies a source-code link. Hardware, software versions, hyperparameter searches, implementation equations and pseudocode are otherwise substantially retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of graph extrapolation, fairness, causality and training dynamics, and adds references including A-DGNs, CDE and Van Loan's matrix-exponential analysis. Several general invariant-learning references disappear. These update the research context while retaining the central positioning around topological generalization.

P1.justification: The title, model terminology, abstract and introduction are extensively revised. The narrative changes from analyzing existing diffusion models before introducing ADiT to presenting AdvDIFFormer before comparator analysis. Proof appendices are reorganized, the contents and reproducibility statement disappear, an impact statement is added, and the outlook moves to Appendix G.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. The architecture illustration is redrawn and moved from Figure 2 to Figure 1; synthetic plots receive new axes and captions. Protein tables are restructured, several tables disappear, and retained molecular examples and sensitivity plots are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical precision by including the previously omitted label-shift term and replacing commutativity-based proof steps; additional baselines and worst-case reporting also help. However, molecular-screening claims and dataset listings remain after their supporting results disappear. Substantially revised protein RMSEs lack an explanation, while sensitivity plots retain v1's values and scale. These competing changes in rigor, evidential support and traceability prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
